parts.article:
Ambergris
 
What is it and where does it come from?
 
(A) In the ancient world, the waxy grey substance we now refer to as ambergris was highly prized for its medicinal properties, and was widely used as a spice, which was believed to be an aphrodisiac when added to food or wine. Ambergris itself is pleasantly aromatic, especially when warmed, and it was also highly valued as a fixing agent in the making of perfume, since it enabled a scent to retain its fragrance for much longer than might otherwise have been possible. Most ambergris was found in the form of lumps floating on the surface of the sea, or washed up on the shores of tropical and temperate oceans. At one time, ambergris was worth its weight in gold, but there was much confusion about its origins.
 
(B) Ambergris was known to the Arabs as 'ambar' and was originally called amber in the West in the Middle Ages. This eventually led to further confusion in the popular mind between ambergris and true amber, the mineral known to mineralogists as succinite, which is actually fossilised tree resin, and generally yellow in colour. Both substances were rare and costly, and both were associated with the sea, largely because for Europeans the most common source of amber was the shores of the Baltic. In Chapter 92 of Moby Dick, the American writer Herman Melville pours scorn on those who believed the two substances to be the same: 'Though the word ambergris is but the French compound for grey amber, yet the two substances are quite distinct. For amber, though at times found on the sea-coast, is also dug up in some far-inland soils, whereas ambergris is never found except upon the sea. Besides, amber is a hard, transparent, brittle, odourless substance, used for mouth-pieces to pipes, for beads and ornaments; but ambergris is soft, waxy, and so highly fragrant that it is largely used in perfumery.'
 
(C) Moby Dick was published in 1851, by which time the mystery of the origins of ambergris had been resolved by the scientific community. In 1783, the botanist Joseph Banks, who had accompanied Captain James Cook on his voyages of discovery in the Pacific, presented a paper to the Royal Society of London by the German physician Dr Franz Xavier Schwediawer in which it was conclusively proved that ambergris came from sperm whales. In this, he was confirming an observation made in the 13ᵗʰ century by the great Venetian traveller Marco Polo who, while on the island of Socotra in the Indian Ocean, had witnessed a sperm whale vomiting up ambergris. But whereas Marco Polo imagined that the whale had swallowed the lump in the depths of the sea, Schwediawer showed that the origin of the material was inside the whale itself.
 
(D) The sperm whale is the largest of the odontocetes, or toothed whales. Males can grow up to 20 metres in length. Melville described the sperm whale as 'the king of whales', and his novel Moby Dick is based on the pursuit of one such creature. Sperm whales are renowned for their ability to dive to great depths, possibly as far as 3 000 metres below the surface, and for remaining underwater for periods of two hours or more in pursuit of their favourite prey, the giant squid. It is from the problems the whales have in digesting the beaks of such creatures that ambergris has its origins. The beak is sharp and irritates the whale's lower intestine, which responds by producing a black, foul-smelling liquid. It is not clear to scientists whether this secretion should be considered a normal response by the whale's digestive system or a pathological one, but from time to time large quantities of the liquid are vomited up by the whale. Once outside the whale's body and exposed to air, the substance hardens, acquiring the waxy, greyish and pleasantly aromatic characteristics of ambergris. Often the beaks of squid are still found embedded in lumps of ambergris, some of which can weigh several hundred kilograms. Melville took some delight in contrasting the origins of ambergris with the high value placed upon it by refined society: 'Who would think, then, that such fine ladies and gentlemen should regale themselves with an essence found in the inglorious bowels of a sick whale!'
 
(E) Sperm whales were ruthlessly pursued by commercial whalers in the 19ᵗʰ and 20ᵗʰ centuries. In 1963-64 alone, almost 30 000 individuals were killed, and only the imposition of a ban on the hunting of sperm whales in 1984 saved the species from extinction. Ambergris was by far the most valuable product to be extracted during the processing of the whales' carcasses, and over 90 per cent of the annual worldwide total was acquired in this way, as a by-product of commercial whaling. However, even before the ban on hunting sperm whales was imposed, the 1972 Marine Mammal Protection Act had prohibited trade in ambergris. Just as petroleum and plastic products were replacing other natural products of whaling, so ambergris was supplanted in the making of perfume by other materials, some natural and some synthetic in origin. Nevertheless, it is possible that, as sperm-whale populations recover to their former numbers in the wild, so the sight of lumps of ambergris washed ashore along the tide-line will once again become a familiar one to beachcombers the world over.

reference:
Q1

干扰 只要文中提到两者都贵（costly/worth gold），那就是Both，不要只盯着其中一个看。

句子 (Paragraph B) "Both substances were rare and costly..."

解析 A段说龙涎香曾“worth its weight in gold（价值连城）”，B段说两种物质都“rare and costly（稀有且昂贵）”，所以两者皆是，选 C。

Q2

解析 A段提到龙涎香被用作“spice（香料）”添加到食物或酒中，而琥珀没有这种用途，选 A。

干扰 “Spice”在这里就是一种调味品（food flavouring），仅用于描述ambergris。

句子 (Paragraph A) "...and was widely used as a spice... when added to food or wine."

Q3

解析 全文虽然提到它们很贵（worth its weight in gold），但从未说它们被直接当做“货币（currency）”来流通使用，选 D。

干扰 “值钱”不等于“当作钱用”，文中没有 currency 或 money 的直接使用描述。

Q4

干扰 “Sweet-smelling”对应“aromatic/fragrant”，而琥珀明确是无味的。

解析 A段说龙涎香是“pleasantly aromatic（芳香宜人）”，B段Melville说琥珀是“odourless（无味）”而龙涎香是“highly fragrant（高度芳香）”，选 A。

句子 (Paragraph B) "...amber is... odourless substance... but ambergris is... highly fragrant..."

Q5

解析 B段引用了Herman Melville在《白鲸》中的话，他同时提到了ambergris和amber并进行了对比，选 C。

干扰 文中那段引言（quotation）里两个词都出现了，显然是两者都被提及。

句子 (Paragraph B) "...Herman Melville pours scorn... 'Though the word ambergris is but the French compound for grey amber...'"

Q6

解析 B段Melville描述琥珀是“transparent（透明的）”，即可以看穿，而龙涎香是“waxy（蜡状的/不透明）”，选 B。

干扰 “Can be seen through” 是 “transparent” 的通俗解释。

句子 (Paragraph B) "...amber is a hard, transparent, brittle... substance..."

Q7

句子 (Paragraph D) "It is from the problems the whales have in digesting the beaks of such creatures that ambergris has its origins."

干扰 题目中的“problems digesting”对应原文的“problems they have in digesting”，后面紧跟核心名词。

解析 题目说龙涎香形成是因为消化巨型乌贼的____有问题，原文D段提到是由于消化这些生物的“beaks（喙/嘴）”产生的问题，填 beaks。

Q8

解析 题目说黑色液体产生并不时被____，原文D段说大量的液体被鲸鱼“vomited up（呕吐出来）”，填 vomited up。

干扰 题目是被动语态“is ______”，原文同样是被动“are vomited up”，直接照抄动词短语。

句子 (Paragraph D) "...from time to time large quantities of the liquid are vomited up by the whale."

Q9

解析 题目说液体接触空气后会____，原文D段说一旦暴露在空气中，物质“hardens（变硬）”，填 hardens。

干扰 “On contact with the air” 对应原文的 “exposed to air”。

句子 (Paragraph D) "Once outside the whale's body and exposed to air, the substance hardens..."

Q10

干扰 “Processing dead whales” 对应 “processing of the whales' carcasses”，“most” 对应 “over 90 per cent”。

解析 题目说20世纪大部分龙涎香来自处理死鲸。原文E段说“over 90 per cent（超过90%）”是通过处理鲸鱼尸体（processing carcasses）获得的，即作为商业捕鲸的副产品，选 TRUE。

句子 (Paragraph E) "...over 90 per cent of the annual worldwide total was acquired in this way, as a by-product of commercial whaling."

Q11

解析 原文E段只提到龙涎香曾是最有价值的产品，后来被替代，但并没有提到“最近（recently）”它的价值是否“增加（increased）”，选 NOT GIVEN。

干扰 哪怕你知道现在龙涎香很贵，也要基于原文，文中没有“最近价值上涨”的信息。

Q12

解析 题目说龙涎香仍然是香水的重要成分。原文E段说龙涎香在香水制作中已经被其他材料（合成或天然）“supplanted（取代/代替）”了，选 FALSE。

干扰 “Supplanted” 意味着被替换掉了，不再是“remains an important ingredient”。

句子 (Paragraph E) "...so ambergris was supplanted in the making of perfume by other materials..."

Q13

解析 题目说最近发现了龙涎香的新用途。文中只提到了旧用途（药、香料、香水）和现在的替代情况，未提及“New uses（新用途）”，选 NOT GIVEN。

干扰 “新发现”在文中仅限于其来源（Schweidawer的发现），而非用途。
